items.q: What does he mean by the wiggle?
items.a: The feeling that **moves a room** when people make music together. A straight line is a **Roman road or a clock hand**: set, and brittle. A wiggle is **water**. It changes shape. He quotes Alan Watts: **no straight lines in nature**.

items.q: What is music, in this talk?
items.a: **Wiggling air.** Players keep moving: high to low, loud to quiet, thick to thin. The skill is learned **through play**.

items.q: What is a melody doing on this song?
items.a: Drawing a line that **tells a story**. Armstrong's "trees of green" is the tree, the sky, the little cloud, **the sun going down**. A flat reading is the version he rejects.

items.q: Why does he stop the even reading?
items.a: Rhythm is **time in the body**. He sings the pocket. He says he just watched the room move with him. Then the line has **space, form, and dynamics** to talk to.

items.q: How can one pitch change color?
items.a: On **"And I think to myself"** the melody note stays. The chord that could have stayed **moves**. He says the note completely changed color. A chord can **squint, reassure, enchant, purify, or terrify**.

items.q: Why is the last home better?
items.a: The song left home, went warm, then dark, then lighter, then sadder. Coming back is more beautiful **because the line traveled**. The story is **tension, release, dissonance, consonance**.

items.q: What should you do when life feels like a straight line?
items.a: **Be a wiggler.** Harmony is not everyone on the same note. Time is not stepping into line. Being in tune is not being perfect. **Yield and soften, or stiffen and break.** He says you already know how.
